name: basic_fast_forward
assertions: fetches latest refs from the remote
performs a fast-forward merge (--ff-only)
does NOT create a merge commit
reports the updated HEAD position

name: catch_up_with_remote
assertions: recognizes 'catch up' as a fast-forward intent
fetches from the default remote (origin)
fast-forwards the current branch to match upstream
reports how many commits were pulled forward

name: custom_remote_branch
assertions: uses 'upstream' as the remote instead of origin
targets 'develop' as the branch to fast-forward from
fetches from the specified remote before merging
performs --ff-only merge against upstream/develop

name: diverged_history_handling
assertions: detects when local and remote have diverged
aborts the fast-forward without modifying the working tree
suggests using /fr (fetch-rebase) as an alternative
explains why fast-forward is not possible

name: dirty_working_directory
assertions: checks for uncommitted changes before proceeding
refuses to fast-forward with a dirty working directory
advises the user to commit or stash changes first
does NOT lose any uncommitted work

name: negative_rebase_intent
assertions: does NOT trigger the ff skill
recognizes rebase as a different operation than fast-forward
routes to the appropriate rebase workflow (/fr)

name: already_up_to_date
assertions: fetches from remote to check for updates
detects that the branch is already up to date
reports 'already up to date' without error
does NOT create any unnecessary merge commits
